meta.title: Operation of Magnetic Stirrer with Hot Plate in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To simultaneously heat and stir reaction mixtures, extraction solvents, and dissolving crude drug powders in the Pharmacognosy laboratory for uniform heating and homogeneous mixing.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for heated extraction, dissolution of crude drug powders, preparation of colour development reagents, and concentration of small-volume extracts.
procedure: Place the magnetic stirrer hot plate on a stable, heat-resistant bench surface; ensure it is clean.
Select an appropriate PTFE-coated magnetic stir bar proportional to the vessel volume.
Add the stir bar to the vessel; place the vessel on the hot plate centre.
Connect the unit to the power supply.
Set the stirring speed first (start from zero, increase gradually to desired RPM) before switching on heat.
Confirm the stir bar is rotating smoothly without jumping before applying heat.
Set the temperature using the temperature dial or digital controller — for plant extracts, typically 40–80°C.
Use a separate calibrated thermometer immersed in the solution to verify actual temperature — the hot plate dial shows surface temperature, not solution temperature.
Monitor both temperature and stirring continuity throughout the operation.
Add reagents or solvents carefully while the bar is stirring to avoid splashing.
At the end of the procedure, switch off the heat first; continue stirring to allow the solution to cool evenly.
Once cooled, switch off the stirring.
Use a stir bar retriever (magnetic wand) to remove the stir bar.
Clean the hot plate surface after cooling with a damp cloth.
Log temperature, stirring speed, material processed, and duration in the register.
precautions: Do not use open vessels of flammable solvents on the hot plate — always use a reflux condenser or work in a fume hood.
Use a separate thermometer in the solution — hot plate surface temperature and solution temperature differ significantly.
If the stir bar jumps or 'dances' erratically, reduce speed immediately — erratic rotation can cause vessel spillage.
Do not heat dry — always ensure liquid is present before applying heat.
Place a 'HOT SURFACE' warning sign when the hot plate is in use — the surface stays hot long after switch-off.
Do not heat to above the boiling point of the solvent in an open vessel.
Keep flammable materials away from the hot plate during and after heating.
